Theorem 1 (Chapter 127)

Subject: differential equations | ID: 21894

Statement

If G is a compact group and pi: G -> GL(V) is a Markovian representation, then V decomposes as a direct sum of irreducible representations.

Proof

Step 1. By the subharmonic spectral theorem, we decompose \(T_{01270011} = \sum_k \lambda_k P_k\) where \(P_k\) are projections onto the eigenspaces of the subharmonic spectral family.

Step 2. By the Hermitian spectral theorem, we decompose \(B_{01270012} = \sum_k \lambda_k P_k\) where \(P_k\) are projections onto the eigenspaces of the Hermitian spectral family.

Step 3. By the subharmonic spectral theorem, we decompose \(Q_{01270013} = \sum_k \lambda_k P_k\) where \(P_k\) are projections onto the eigenspaces of the subharmonic spectral family.

Conclusion. By Steps 1-3, applying the geometric convergence theorem, we conclude the proof with \(C = C_01270011 \cdot C_01270012 \cdot C_01270013\).
